Slips: the opening clause (མྱང་)འདས་བྱེད་པོ་ལས་ཀྱང་མེད (no nirvāṇa, no agent, no action) is garbled as 'even from nirvana there would be no agent'; ཤེས་བྱ་ཤེས་པ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར (both known and knowing absent) is distorted to 'does not exist without the consciousness'.

inventions.quote: Is an untenable thought.

reason: Prasannapadā on MMK 22.12–14 rendered faithfully: the four views on the prior and later limit, the opponent's ལུང་དུ་མ་བསྟན་པ objection, the four views on the nirvāṇa'd Tathāgata. The verse ends at བསམ་པ་འཐད་པ; the negation ('untenable', ཉིད་མི་འགྱུར) comes from the next side.

MMK 2.13b–3.2 rendered verse by verse with correct polarity, incl. colophon of ch.2. Minor slips: opening འགྲོ་བ་ག་ལ་ཡོད (how can going exist) as 'how can a goer exist'; in 2.22 'motion does not exist prior to the goer' reverses which term is prior (the goer does not exist before going).

Whole side rendered in order: the Buddhas' blessing and Vimukticandra's point, the two kinds of certainty (ripening/action) beyond the Buddhas' power, glosses of རི་མོའི་ཡི་གེ/ཡི་གེའི་འབྲུ/གྲངས/བསྟན་པ/ཡི་གེའི་ཕྱི་མོ, both request verses, and the realization/scripture analysis to རབ་མཆོག་ཉིད་དེ. Note is a plain explanation.

inventions.quote: means not being dependent on death and birth

reason: Gandharva/thrice passage, the Vibhaṅga citation and the word-glosses are rendered correctly, but the opening clause (ཀྱང་ཆེས་ཤས་ཆེ་བར་གྱུར་ཏེ) is dropped, and དགེ་འདུན་གྱི་དབྱེན་ལ་སོགས་པར་བཟློག་པར་ཡལ་བར་གཞག་པ (neglecting to prevent schism) is distorted to 'remain indifferent to avoid a schism'; the closing gloss verb (མི་ལྟོས་པ) is on the next side.

inversion_quotes.english: This is quite possible in a town, despite the many immediate distractions.
inversion_quotes.should_be: A town is not [such a cause], because of its many immediate activities.

reason: Both sets of four ཚོགས་དང་མཐུན་པའི་ཆོས and their bases are rendered accurately (Sudhana, བཟོད་པ་དང་དེས་པ, དགོན་པ), but the sentence excluding the town is reversed into an affirmation that practice is 'quite possible in a town'.

inversion_quotes.english: "Great" refers to the ultimate truth. "Vajra" refers to the relative truth.
inversion_quotes.should_be: "Great" is the relative truth; "vajra" is the ultimate truth.

reason: Rest of the side (fourth instruction, illusory body, dharmakāya as clear light, self-consecration, compiler's words, Akṣobhya etc., reason/thesis on illusion) is rendered faithfully, but the gloss on རྡོ་རྗེ་འཆང་ཆེན་པོ swaps relative and ultimate truth; Esukhia '#' collation marks are copied into the English four times.
